title: Independently verify recovered key-pair public/private consistency
why: L109's direct-reuse test requires source-valid recovered key material. Earlier E361/j335 verified metadata and lengths only, not public/private consistency. Independently re-derive public keys with examiner-written finite-field arithmetic, without printing scalars or performing DBX key/codec trials.
product: Sealed per-record boolean source-consistency report, with no key scalar/hash values.
acceptance: Algorithm controls pass; all four typed records examined; failures reported individually and no DBX-role conclusion asserted.

routes.method: Decode the four typed private/public records offline, derive public bytes by pure-Python arithmetic and compare only boolean equality results. Validate the implementation against trusted-library deterministic synthetic controls; secret output sealed.
Read established item/type/length metadata to ensure the same four original records are examined; do not use summaries as substitute scalar inputs.

overlap_why: A separate mathematical implementation of Ed25519/X25519 public derivation checks L109's source-key consistency control; it does not duplicate DBX authentication trials or earlier metadata-only parsing.
next_action: Read the sanitized metadata, then run one independent secret-output mathematical validation job.
